description.narrative:
The objective of this support is Building Inclusive and Multi-dimensional Approaches and Capacities for Effective Conflict Prevention in Africa.
The intervention covers 3 result areas: 1) Enhanced Institutional Responses of the AU and RECS to Prevent Complex Conflicts 2) Strengthened Capacities of National and Local Infrastructures for Effective Conflict Prevention 3) Enhanced Evidence Based Analysis to Inform Policy Support and Knowledge Production for Conflict Prevention
Key constituencies to the programme include local, national, and regional structures, such as the AU, RECs/RMs (IGAD, SADC, ECCAS), and other organisations such as the United Cities and Local Governments; Youth focused and youth-led organisations, Women focused, and women led organisations and Networks (FemWise-Africa and GIMAC); Community leaders; and Faith-based and traditional leaders.

sector.narrative: Civilian peace-building, conflict prevention and resolution

title.narrative: African Centre for the Constructive Resolution of Dispute (ACCORD)

description.narrative:
Key deliverables according to ACCORD has been the continued work with Femwise-South Sudan local chapter that resulted in the launch of the network. In addition, ACCORD has continued the consultations with AU mediation unit regarding the revision of the AU Mediation Handbook which is an important institutional tool for AU:s work on mediation.
On a regional level ACCORD has engaged with SADC in its work to develop a strategy for Youth Peace and Security. ACCORD has supported the review of the strategy to pave the way for its validation and eventuell adoption in 2025.
On a South African level, ACCORD has worked with local NGO:s with the Women Peace and Security Agenda. ACCORD has contributed to the establishment of a National Action Plan (NAP) for UNSCR 1325. In 2024, ACCORD has continued this work to establish local awareness, knowledge and capacity development with regards to the NAP.
ACCORD has deepened its engagement with the Council of Swaziland Churches to strenghten the role of faith based leaders in conflict prevention. The aim of this cooperation is to establish Local Peace Committees with the aim of contributing to a local infrastructure for conflict prevention in a politically volatile environment.
These are some examples of how ACCORD has worked with conflict prevention in various processes and levels (regional, national and local) and with various actors (AU, faith based organisations and local NGO:s).
